label: prop:phi-q-aj-machinery-identification
title: $\Phi_q$ / $\mathrm{Li}_2^q$ machinery is the AJ-conjecture machinery
html:
Conditional on Quantum Langlands duality — H_n(q) ↔ H_n(q^{-1}) via Cartan folding (Type A_{n-1} ↔ {}^L\!A_{n-1}) + Ding–Iohara–Miki master Pentagon as unified ancestor of Macdonald + q-dilog Pentagons.

Let K be a hyperbolic knot or link with quantum A-polynomial \hat{A}_K \in \mathcal{A}_q (the q-Weyl algebra over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]), defined from the recursion of the colored Jones function [garoufalidis2004, §2.2]. The \Phi_q (Faddeev) and \mathrm{Li}_2^q (Rogers) asymptotic regulators appearing in the framework are specific saddle-point regimes of the AJ machinery

  \hat{A}_K(\hat{L}, \hat{M}; q) \cdot J_N(K; q) \;=\; 0 :

namely \Phi_q is its root-of-unity saddle (q = e^{2\pi i / N}) and \mathrm{Li}_2^q its real saddle (q \in (0, 1)). The identification is algebraic over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] on both sides; the two contexts differ only by the choice of archimedean saddle.

The full AJ-conjecture statement, the significance of the unified context-sorting, and the logical structure of the conditional proposition are recorded in the details note.

Sources for the two readings. The Chern--Simons reading of the root-of-unity saddle comes from Gukov, who identifies the zero locus of the A-polynomial with a Lagrangian submanifold of the \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) Chern--Simons phase space [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §3.1] and states the generalised volume conjecture: a one-parameter family of colored-Jones asymptotics \mathrm{Vol}(l,m) + i\,2\pi^2\,\mathrm{CS}(l,m) on that zero locus, which contains the volume conjecture at m = 1 [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.2, eq. (5.12)]; for 4_1 the source checks the real part [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.3]. Dimofte and Gukov extend the leading term to the full expansion in \hbar = i\pi/k [dimofte-gukov2010, §2.2, eqs. (2.15)--(2.17)] and treat \hat A_K as the quantisation of the A-polynomial [dimofte-gukov2010, §3.2]. Hikami assigns Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm to each ideal tetrahedron of a cusped hyperbolic manifold, shows that the classical limit of the resulting invariant is the Neumann--Zagier potential, and derives the A-polynomial from that potential [hikami2006, Abstract and §1]. On the algebraic side, Takata proves that for every twist knot the A-polynomial is recovered from the q = 1 specialisation of the recurrences satisfied by the summand of Masbaum's colored-Jones formula [takata2004, Thm. 2.2], and relates this to the AJ conjecture, recording a computer-algebra observation of the same for 5_2 and 6_1 [takata2004, §4]. These sources give the setting of the conditional inputs; none of them discharges those inputs.
